### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, the six activities A33, A35, A36, A37, A38 and A39 each ran in every case (200 of 200 traces). In the later window, A33, A35 and A36 run in about 47 in 100 cases (93–94 of 200) and A37, A38 and A39 in about 56–57 in 100 cases (112–113 of 200). [OCC031, OCC033, OCC034, OCC035, OCC036, OCC037]
- Earlier, every case contained both groups, with the A33/A35/A36 group always before the A37/A38/A39 group (about 99 in 100 cases). In the later window the two groups have become almost mutually exclusive: pairs spanning the groups co-occur in only about 3 in 100 cases (for example A33 with A37 falls from 1.00 to 0.03). [REL016, REL018, REL020, REL022, REL023, REL025]
- Within each group the three activities still run together as a block, but for a within-group pair about 42–54 in 100 later cases contain neither activity — these are the cases that took the other group. The mixed order inside each group is unchanged between the windows. [REL014, REL019, REL026, REL027, REL028]
- The surrounding activities are unchanged: A30 and A31 still occur in every case in both windows, and A30 still precedes A31 in about 99 in 100 cases. [OCC029, POS001, POS002, REL001]
- The bypass is visible directly in the edges: A33, A35 and A36, which earlier never led to A31, now lead straight to A31 in about 26–34 in 100 of their outgoing transitions, and A30 now feeds both groups instead of only the first. [DIR033, DIR035, DIR036, DIR030]
- Event-position distances shrink accordingly: the gap from A30 to A37/A38/A39 and from A33/A35/A36 to A31 moves from 4–5 steps earlier to 1–3 steps later, and mean relative positions shift (A30 from about 0.62 to 0.67, A31 from about 0.82 to 0.80), consistent with a shorter middle block. [LAG004, LAG006, LAG007, LAG013, LAG019, POS001, POS002]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that the six-activity block between A30 and A31 is no longer executed in full in every case: in the later window a case typically runs exactly one half of the block — about 46 in 100 cases run A33, A35 and A36 and then continue directly to A31, skipping A37, A38 and A39, while about 54 in 100 run A37, A38 and A39 and skip A33, A35 and A36; only about 3 in 100 still run both halves, in the earlier fixed order. A30 and A31 behave as before. The signs are direct and consistent across indicator families: participation of all six activities drops from 100% to 47–57%, with differences larger than in about 995 of 1,000 random re-splits; cross-group co-occurrence collapses from certainty to about 3 in 100; new direct edges to A31 appear where none were observed; and inter-activity distances shorten. These families largely describe the same underlying trace change, so they agree but are not independent confirmations. The main competing explanation the evidence cannot rule out is a shift in the mix of case types between the two windows rather than a modification of the process, and the evidence cannot show what determines which half a case runs. The evidence set also does not report how many qualifying items an unchanged process would produce, so this judgement rests on the size and coherence of the effects. [OCC031, OCC033, OCC034, OCC035, OCC036, OCC037, REL016, REL023, DIR033, DIR035, DIR036, LAG004, LAG007, POS001, POS002]

Other differences: A44 occurs more often (participation about 63 in 100 cases earlier vs 68 in 100 later; mean occurrences 0.80 vs 0.94) and A43 repeats more (mean 1.55 vs 1.72 occurrences per case); A02 occurs less often (about 20 in 100 cases earlier vs 13 in 100 later); A21 and A23 occur somewhat less and A22 and A24 somewhat more (shifts of about 5–7 in 100 cases). A48's successor profile changed completely, but it rests on only 8 versus 5 observed outgoing transitions, so it is weak. [OCC042, OCC041, OCC002, OCC021, OCC022, OCC023, OCC024, DIR048]
